correctness.summary: The support-function Fourier proof gives the coefficient 2π from the exact odd-mode evaluation sum 1/4; a finite smooth constant-width Fourier family makes the ratio of area deficit to squared Steiner-disk Hausdorff distance tend to 2π, and the equality profile is excluded by curvature-measure positivity.

limitations: Only planar Euclidean constant-width convex bodies are treated.
Sharpness concerns distance to the Steiner disk, not optimization over all translated disks.
The noncircular sharp constant is approached by smooth examples rather than attained.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an equivalent result may exist under different support-function or Sobolev terminology.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Groemer's 1988 Hausdorff stability theorem, later constant-width stability/asymmetry literature, Steiner-disk Fourier deficit work, and a current Fourier treatment of constant-width bodies were checked. No located source states the sharp canonical Steiner-disk inequality or its smooth sharpness family; equivalent older formulations remain a residual risk.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result sharpens a classical disk-stability estimate, fixes a canonical comparison disk, determines the optimal constant for that distance, and explains nonattainment outside the disk.
